newsitem.title: FINLAND: END TO BANK LOAN STAMP DUTY NOT IN BUDGET - NIINISTO.
newsitem.headline: END TO BANK LOAN STAMP DUTY NOT IN BUDGET - NIINISTO.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Wednesday that a removal of the stamp duty on bank loans had not been budgeted for 1998.
"It is absolutely out of the question, there is no such item in the 1998 budget frames," Niinisto told reporters after a briefing on Wednesday.
Finnish media on Tuesday quoted second Finance Minister Arja Alho as saying that the stamp duty on bank loans would be scrapped starting next year.
The 700 million markka loss in annual state revenue from the stamp duty would be compensated by raising income from value added tax, Alho was quoted as saying.
But Niinisto said the loss in revenue would be closer to one billlion markka than 700 million.
"I am responsible for the budget, Alho is responsible for what she says," Niinisto said, when asked whether it was true that stamp duty on bank loans will be removed.
